faq.question: What does Raashid mean?
faq.answer: Raashid is associated with the Arabic form رَاشِد, whose core sense is raashid; rightly guided.

faq.question: What is the origin of Raashid?
faq.answer: Raashid is associated with Arabic. Raashid is Arabic رَاشِد (Rāshid) 'rightly guided', from the root ر ش د (r-sh-d). The source gloss 'Rightly Guided' is consistent. Same name as rachid.

faq.question: Is Raashid an Arabic name?
faq.answer: Yes — the underlying form رَاشِد is Arabic.

faq.question: Is Raashid an Islamic name?
faq.answer: Raashid can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.answer: Raashid should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. False

faq.question: What does Raashid mean in Persian?
faq.answer: In Persian, Raashid is rendered راشد and carries the sense راشد، هدایت‌یافته.

faq.answer: A romanized syllable approximation is raas-hid. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.answer: Romanization variants include Raashid, raashid, rashid. Script forms are راشد, رَاشِد, राशिद.
